title: Turtle Soup
description: A soup made with turtle, ham, and veal.
steps: Cut off the head of the turtle the preceding day
In the morning open the turtle by leaning heavily with a knife on the shell of the animal's back and cut this off all round
Turn it upright on its end that all the water may run out
Cut the flesh off along the spine with the knife sloping towards the bones to avoid touching the gall
Wash the flesh clean and let them drain
Have ready a large vessel full of boiling water and put the shells into it
When the shells come easily off take them out of the water and prick them all including those of the back belly fins and head
Boil the back and belly till the bones can be taken off without allowing the softer parts to be sufficiently done as they will be boiled again in the soup
Lay the slices of ham on the bottom of a very large stewpan over them the knuckles of veal then the inside flesh of the turtle and over the whole the members
Moisten with the water in which you are boiling the shell and draw it down thoroughly
Ascertain if it be thoroughly done by thrusting a knife into the fleshy part of the meat
When no blood appears moisten it again with the liquor in which the bones have been boiling
Put in a large bunch of sweet herbs--sweet basil sweet marjoram lemon thyme winter savory 2 or 3 bay-leaves common thyme a handful of parsley and green onions and a large onion stuck with 6 cloves
Let the whole be thoroughly done
Probe the members to see whether they are done and if so drain and send them to the larder
When the flesh is completely done strain it through a silk sieve
Make a very thin white roux with flour
Moisten the roux with the liquor keeping it over the fire till it boils
Ascertain that the sauce is neither too thick nor too thin
Draw the stewpan on the side of the stove to skim off the white scum and all the fat and oil that rise to the surface
Cut the softer parts to about the size of one or two inches square and throw into the soup
Let the soup simmer gently
Skim off all the fat and froth
Take all the leaves of the herbs from the stock and put these in a stewpan with about 1/4 lb. of fresh butter
Let it simmer on a slow fire till quite melted
Pour in 1 bottle of good Madeira adding a small bit of sugar and let it boil gently for 1 hour
Rub it through a tammy and add it to the soup
Let the soup boil till no white scum rises
Take with a skimmer all the bits of turtle out of the sauce and put them in a clean stewpan
Pour the soup over the bits of turtle through a tammy
Make quenelles à tortue by taking the fleshy part of a leg of veal about 1 lb. scraping off all the meat without leaving any sinews or fat
Soak in milk about the same quantity of crumbs of bread
Squeeze the bread and put it into a mortar with the veal a small quantity of calf's udder a little butter the yolks of 4 eggs boiled hard a little cayenne pepper salt and spices
Pound the whole very fine
Thicken the mixture with 2 whole eggs and the yolk of another
Try this farce or stuffing in boiling-hot water to ascertain its consistency
If it is too thin add the yolk of an egg
Take half of the farce and put into it some chopped parsley
Let the whole cool in order to roll it of the size of the yolk of an egg
Poach it in salt and boiling water and when very hard drain on a sieve and put it into the turtle
Before you send up squeeze the juice of 2 or 3 lemons with a little cayenne pepper and pour that into the soup
When either lemon-juice or cayenne pepper has been introduced no boiling must take place

title: Vanilla Cream
description: Prepared with vanilla, isinglass, and milk.
steps: Put the milk and sugar into a saucepan, and let it get hot over a slow fire.

Flavour the whole with essence of vanilla, put the mixture into a jug, and place this jug in a saucepan of boiling water.
Stir the contents with a wooden spoon one way until the mixture thickens, but do not allow it to boil, or it will be full of lumps.
Take it off the fire; stir in the isinglass, which should be previously dissolved in about 1/4 pint of water, and boiled for 2 or 3 minutes.
Pour the cream into an oiled mould, put it in a cool place to set, and turn it out carefully on a dish.

steps: Take large cucumbers or melons, such as are green, put them into a jar of strong salt and water, with vine leaves on the top

Put them on a slow fire in alum and water, covered with vine leaves

Put them in cold spring water, changing it twice a day for three days
Have ready a syrup made as follows: To one pound of loaf sugar add half an ounce of powdered ginger, and as much water as will moisten it
Boil it and skim it well
When it is quite free from scum and boiling fast, add the juice and rind of a lemon
When this syrup is quite cold pour it over the cucumber or melon
Should the syrup be too thin after standing two or three days, boil it again with a little more sugar

steps: Dissolve 3 pounds raw finely crushed cream of tartar in some must and add this solution to 120 pounds of apple must in a barrel

title: Almut eingefänzent (Sauerkraut)
description: Prepared with cabbage, caraway seeds, and salt.
steps: Let the cabbage heads lie for 8 days or longer to ferment

Slice the cabbage with a cabbage plane or knife onto a clean cloth
Line the bottom of the barrel or tub with cabbage leaves
Sprinkle with salt mixed with caraway seeds
Add hand-height pieces of cabbage, then salt and caraway again, and continue this process
When the barrel is half full, stamp down the cabbage very firmly with a wooden pestle or by foot
Ensure the cabbage forms an even surface without any indentations
Continue filling and stamping in this manner
When the barrel is full and salt and caraway are sprinkled on top, stamp again
Cover with cabbage leaves and place a fitting lid on top, weighting it down with stones
If using a special barrel, drill two holes one finger width below the rim and insert a tube so excess water can drain off
If using a screw barrel, the screw must be tightened daily
After three weeks, when the cabbage is already edible, skim off the foam and water, rinse the cabbage well, cover and weight it, and pour fresh water over so it stands hand-high above the cabbage
Each time cabbage is removed, take it evenly so no indentations form, then cover, weight, and pour fresh water over
Wash the cabbage, lid, and stones every 8 days
Cabbage can be stored 1-2 years

title: Apfel-Charlotte (Apple Charlotte)
description: Prepared with apples, marmalade, and flour.
steps: Prepare a butter dough of finest quality from 28 Deka flour (No. 1035) and let it rest covered in a cool place

Meanwhile prepare the filling: peel about 24 cooking apples, remove the core casings, cut the apples into wedges and put them in a casserole, sweeten as desired and steam covered without water or other liquid until no liquid remains
Add some spoonfuls of desired marmalade, stir well together and let it come to a boil once, then set aside and let cool

Brush the dough with the cold apple marmalade leaving a thumb-width border free on all 4 sides, brush this border with beaten egg
Roll the second part of the rolled out butter dough onto the strudel roller and unroll it over the apples so that the edges lie evenly together and the side that was on the board comes on top
Lightly press the edges together, make shallow cuts in the upper dough layer with a knife, brush the dough with beaten egg but leave the edges knife-back-width dry
Place these prepared apple charlottes in the fairly hot oven and bake for 1.5 to 3.5 hours
When the dough is half baked, remove the sheet, sprinkle the dough heavily with finely ground sugar and finish baking

title: Artischocken zu erhalten (Artichokes Preserved)
description: Prepared with artichokes, salt, and water.
steps: Sprinkle salt on the bottom of a clean barrel, place the cut stems of the artichokes upright, reverse the following ones and position them with the tips between the tips of the lower ones, and continue until the barrel is full.

Take a good portion of flowing water and salt, let it boil for quite a long time, and let it cool again, and pour it through the hole into the artichokes.
When the barrel is full, seal the hole firmly with a stopper, place it in the cellar, and shake it occasionally; this way they will keep for a very long time.

title: Aspik (Aspic Jelly)
description: Prepared with calf's head, calf's foot, and pork.
steps: Clean and wash all the meat and ingredients well several times.
Bring to a boil with cleaned, washed, leafy-cut vegetables, onion, bay leaves, peppercorns, spice berries, thyme, salt, and vinegar in an enameled pot with 4 liters of water.
Skim off foam.
Cook slowly for 3 hours, skimming frequently.
Season again to taste with salt and acid.
Cook slowly for another hour.
Strain through a sieve into a vessel.
Let stand until the next day.
Remove the fat from the top with a spoon the next day.
Place the vessel on the heat until the aspic is melted.
Pour into a larger pot; season with a little wine and lemon juice.
Add 6 firm snow and whisk the mass until very hot, almost boiling.
Let the pot stand on the edge of the stove until the aspic settles.
Place an inverted stool on a chair, tie a hot-water-dipped, well-wrung linen cloth or napkin to the 4 feet; place the chair near the stove with a bowl underneath the cloth.
Remove the cloudy, dirty snow from the top of the aspic; pour the aspic spoonful by spoonful onto the cloth.
Do not stir the aspic.
If it is not clear, place another bowl under the cloth and let the aspic run through again.
It must be clear, golden yellow, and slightly sour.
Fill the still-warm aspic into molds rinsed with water.
Let it set in the molds.
To unmold, hold the form in hot water for a moment, or remove with a silver spoon and serve broken into pieces.
Garnish cold fish (such as pike-perch or pike) and goose liver with it; also give to the sick.
For red aspic, add a few drops of beet juice to the molds before filling.

It can be kept for weeks by pouring it into preserving jars, covering them well with parchment paper, letting it set in steam for 1 hour, and storing in a cool place. Otherwise it keeps only 2–3 days.

description: Prepared with veal, bacon, and vinegar.
steps: After trimming the leg and removing the skin, pound it with a meat mallet, rub it with ground spices, lard it with pencil-thick, half-finger-long bacon and let it rest 1 hour.
Meanwhile make a brine of vinegar, water and some wine, add thinly sliced vegetables, 3 bay leaves, cabbage and lemon peel and let it cook well.

Pour this prepared brine over the unsalted leg and let it marinate 2–3 days, during which time drain the brine twice a day, bring it to a boil and pour it cold again over the leg, which should be turned daily.
Before pouring over it the last time, salt both the brine and the leg and let it stand another night.
